method: Read84Japanese paragraphs176–182and source5lPDF9–12body/photos/captions across page boundaries. Compare the selectedk/dceiling-hanger, bolt/nut, demolition-isolation, shock-awareness and tunnel/manhole contexts. Retain common concepts already taught; no whole electrical paragraph imported from a common part name or route metaphor. Word searches navigate only and do not prove complete absence in field sources.

sourceVisualReview.sourceRecognitionNotes: Read source pictures/captions for terminal/ring-sleeve/pin-terminal, push-in connector, earth rod, bolt-support clamp and saddle; distinguish electrical components from bolt/nut/washer and ceiling-framework relationships in k/d. The source image is not copied and does not validate app illustrations.

existingKnowledgeElsewhere.scope: Wall sway restraint and ceiling hanger/load path already explained for building. This does not import the lighting-raceway/insert/electrical-support lesson or change civil scope.
Threaded interfaces, diameter/pitch/system and separate nut versus tapped member already shared. This is not a fresh double-nut tightening rule or product substitution.

sourceSimplificationsAlreadyBounded.scope: Tool handle colors are examples; model/die/wire/terminal fit and verified result remain distinct.
Push-in simplicity and2–3times tape stretch are not adopted as universal operating instructions; conductor types and product conditions remain explicit.
Handhole is not universally a block structure; ladder-only rack and count-only hook/rack selection are not adopted.
Nonbond omission is joint/product specific; hanging does not prove sway restraint, and two nuts do not prove correct tightening.

freshPrimaryReferences.scope: Selected lever-connector family supports multiple conductor constructions under specified model/range conditions; no numbers or wiring sequence copied.
Identified self-amalgamating electrical-insulation product context; not every tape, voltage, waterproof repair or operating method.
Selected rack/joint and BLCbonding configuration description, not a universal all-model conductor-omission rule or full legal compliance statement.

remainingObjectives: Complete reverse source-to-app picture recognition and product-specific conditions, including terminal/tool color conventions and tape construction.
Keep nonbond conductor omission separate from all-system grounding, and supporting hardware separate from structural/seismic approval.
A tunnel-shaft manhole reference does not establish an electrical handhole cable-connection or access objective; full field-source comparison remains open.
